triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix proration multiplied snap_allotment_before_minimum (7 USC 2017(a)) rather than the regulation's calculated monthly allotment before minimums, capped nothing, and handed off to snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance / snap_regular_month_allotment - names the rewritten federal 7 CFR 273.10 module no longer defines - so the initial-month amount was grounded on a stale/other provision, but no tested value actually changed.
triage.triage_notes: Read 10 CCR 2506-1 4.207.2 through the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-07-13): (C) says 'Multiply by the full month's benefits the household is eligible to receive; Divide by the number of days in the application month', and (A) says 'Eligible households are entitled to a full month allotment for all months except an initial month of application' - it does not state a min() cap, and with a proration factor that is <= 1 in every ordinary case the new min(A, floor(A*f)) is a defensive guard that only binds if a public-institution release date precedes the month. The bigger part of this diff is stale-cross-repo-reference repair: the pre-fix test asserted us:regulations/7-cfr/273/10#snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance and #snap_initial_month_minimum_issuance_threshold, and this commit moves the $10 gate into the CO module (formula 'if snap_initial_month_prorated_allotment < snap_initial_month_minimum_issuance: 0 else: ...', matching 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(B) 'less than $10 ... no benefits') while the federal parameter is now snap_initial_month_minimum_issuance. Every expected number in the companion test is unchanged (153, 211, 298, 9 -> 0), which is the main reason I did not call this fidelity. Also adds bridge rules (snap_maximum_allotment_for_household_size, snap_maximum_allotment_for_one_person_household, household_initial_month, and a parameter state_agency_rounds_thirty_percent_net_income_up = false that picks Colorado's rounding option for the federal 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A) branch) and an import of us:statutes/7/2014/e/6/A. A reviewer may want to keep only the re-grounding of the proration base, or prune the whole module.
triage.verifier_justification: The Colorado source (10 CCR 2506-1 4.207.2(C), read through the pinned release) prescribes only "Multiply by the full month's benefits the household is eligible to receive ... Divide by the number of days in the application month" — no cap and no named provision for the base — and both the old base `snap_allotment_before_minimum` (7 USC 2017(a): `floor(max(0, snap_maximum_allotment - snap_household_food_contribution))`) and the new `snap_calculated_monthly_allotment_before_minimums` (7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A), with Colorado's new bridge parameter pinned to the round-down branch: `max(0, floor(...))`) encode the same amount, so the swap re-points at the sibling federal surface rather than correcting meaning. The added `min(...)` is mathematically non-binding under the module's own factor (proration_days ≤ days_in_month ⇒ factor ≤ 1 ⇒ floor(A·factor) ≤ A; I checked all 118 in-month application dates and none differ), and every pre-existing tested value is byte-identical across the commit (153, 211, 298, prorated 9 → allotment 0). The commit is titled "Refresh Colorado SNAP federal references (#3)" and its manifest records `"tool": "axiom-encode repair-colorado-snap-federal-refs"` with `"runner": "deterministic-repair"` — a mechanical rewiring onto the 7 CFR 273.10 module that had been rewritten on 2026-05-12 to stop exporting `snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance` — so the pre-fix text was a dangling cross-module reference, not an encoded meaning that disagrees with 4.207.2.
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation of the first reader on three points. (1) Their quote — "repair initial-month proration and 4.401 separate-household source scope through signed encoder provenance" — appears nowhere in the bundle: the commit body is empty ("\n") and the attached pr_body is PR #395, the monorepo-consolidation PR; I string-searched the JSON for three fragments of it and all were absent, so the classification rests on text that is not in evidence. (2) "Grounded on a stale/other provision" does not hold: `us:statutes/7/2017/a#snap_allotment_before_minimum` still exists and is still asserted at 298 in the POST test file, and the two bases are algebraically identical for Colorado because the commit also adds `state_agency_rounds_thirty_percent_net_income_up: false`, selecting 273.10's `max(0, floor(A - B))` branch, which equals 2017(a)'s `floor(max(0, A - B))`. (3) Their own reading concedes "no tested value actually changed"; I confirmed the six test cases are the same six, with every pre-existing assertion unchanged — the only test edits are renamed federal input keys (`snap_countable_earned_income` → `snap_gross_monthly_earned_income`, `snap_initial_month_minimum_issuance_threshold` → `snap_initial_month_minimum_issuance`) and assertions for the newly added rules. Residual uncertainty that keeps this below 0.8: the min() does bind if `application_date` precedes `period_start` (factor > 1), and 273.10's `snap_net_monthly_income` chain can diverge from 2017(a)'s `snap_net_income_for_allotment` for households with medical/dependent-care/homeless-shelter deductions, so the post version could differ from the pre version in untested richer cases — but that is added precision/scope the module never claimed, which the rubric caps at "unclear", not a source-grounded correction. The four rules with `source: Colorado SNAP federal surface bridge` are adapter plumbing for the rewritten federal module and carry no 4.207.2 citation at all. Reviewer should also note the same deterministic-repair manifest covers the 4.401 file, so a sibling "wrong_entity_or_scope" reading of this commit deserves the same scrutiny.
